info.description:
Training app for climbers. Sign up, sign in on several devices at once, and
sign each one out on its own.

Every failure answers with the same shape: an error object carrying a code,
a human message, and on a validation failure a fields map naming what to
fix.
info.title: Passion

post.description:
Answers with the account and a token, so the client signs up and signs in
with one call.

An address that is already registered answers invalid_credentials, the same
as a wrong password. Telling them apart would let anyone ask the API who has
an account.

get.description: Answers with the account the bearer token belongs to.

The exercises the app ships and the ones you wrote, sorted by name. Retired
ones are left out.

post.description: Adds one to your library. A field left out or sent as null is not set.

get.description: One the app ships or one of yours. A retired one still reads.

put.description:

Finished or not, newest day first.

post.description:
With a template, the run copies it now, so editing the template later never
reaches the run. Without one, it is an open run that starts empty. A
write-up of a day already gone sends that day as local_date.

put.description:
Sets everything but the plan, the template and the finish. A field left out
or sent as null is cleared. A finished run can still be changed.

delete.description: Removes one of your runs with everything logged in it.

put.description:
Creates the climb under the id you chose, or replaces it, so a retry writes
one climb. Its step must be a climbing step the run holds and has not
skipped. A step with a climb counts as done.

parameters.description: The id the client chose for the climb.

parameters.description: The id the client chose for the climb.

post.description:
Every step still null becomes skipped, or done if it has sets or climbs.
Finishing twice keeps the first time.

put.description:
Writes the whole list, so a retry writes the same sets. A step with sets
counts as done. A skipped step keeps no sets, and a climbing step logs
climbs instead. A step the run does not hold answers 404.

parameters.description: The step's id in the run's body.
parameters.name: step

put.description:

post.description:
Takes one of your own out of your list. It still reads by id. Retiring it
twice keeps the first date. A shipped session template, or someone else's,
answers 404.

Each sign-in mints a separate token, so a phone and a laptop hold different
ones and signing out of either leaves the other working.

delete.description:
Deletes the token that authenticated the request. Signing out twice with the
same token answers 401 the second time, because the route authenticates
before it deletes.
